cards.text: After the flood, the nations spread out from Noah's sons (Genesis 10:32), and right now the whole world has one language and a common form of speech. No translator, no subtitles, no "sorry, say that again?" Friend, that's a WONDERFUL world.
People journeying eastward find a wide, flat plain and settle down right there. After years in a junk drawer, baker, a wide open plain sounds like a MANSION to me.

cards.question: Journeying eastward, the people find a plain and settle there. What land is it in?

cards.text: They say to one another, "Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly." Finally, MY word, and baker, I once left a batch in so long those cookies could've held up a wall.

cards.question: To build with those baked bricks, the people use brick instead of ___ and tar instead of ___.

cards.text: Then the plan gets BIGGER. They want to build themselves a city with "a tower that reaches to the heavens" and a whole lot of brick.

cards.question: The people want to build a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens. What do they say it's for?

answers.text: To make a name for themselves
To guard the plain from enemies

cards.question: The people also say building the city with its tower will keep them from being scattered over the face of all the earth.

cards.text: Brick by brick, up it goes, and then the LORD comes down to see the city and the tower. Friend, they built that thing to reach the heavens, and the LORD still came DOWN to see it.
Then the LORD speaks about them: one people, one language, all working on the same thing.

cards.question: The LORD says these people have begun this as one people speaking the same language. What does He say that means?

answers.text: Nothing they plan will be out of their reach
Their city will grow too big for the plain
Their tower will fall before it is finished

cards.question: Then the LORD says, Come, let Us go down. His plan for the builders is to confuse their ___.
When the LORD confuses the builders' language, they won't understand one another's speech.

cards.text: So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, the very thing that city and tower were supposed to prevent. Yeah, THAT one.

cards.question: Once the LORD scatters the people, they keep right on building the city.
The place where the people built their city and tower gets called Babel. Why that name?

answers.text: The LORD confused the language there
The people named it after a king
The name means city of brick

cards.text: And from that place, the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth. Big plans, baker. Bigger God.

findings.problem: The question drops the conditional 'If' from Genesis 11:6 and turns the LORD's statement into an unconditional assertion that the people have begun the work. The retelling needs to preserve the condition.

This non-opening story card has three sentences: the scattering statement, 'Big plans, baker,' and 'Bigger God.' The closing quip needs to be combined into one sentence or otherwise shortened to keep the card within the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
